- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.2), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for risk reversal.
- Model consistently underestimates prices after a spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast for rebound.
- Forecast often lags true price by 1–3 days; adjust for 1-day lead-in if sentiment is trending upward.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–3% unless sentiment is strong bullish.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate late-period prices (last 7–10 days); apply 0.5–1.5% upward adjustment if sentiment is neutral or bullish.
